claims.text: As-built SLM CoCrFeNiMn components inherently contain residual stresses.
As-built SLM CoCrFeNiMn components contain micro-cracks and porosity.
Rapid solidification during SLM causes the stated residual stresses, micro-cracks, and porosity.
Deep cryogenic treatment at approximately -196°C for 2–4 hours followed by controlled warming will induce nano-twins in SLM CoCrFeNiMn.
The proposed deep cryogenic treatment will induce minor secondary-phase transformations.
Cryogenically induced nano-twinning and phase transformations will relieve residual stresses.
Cryogenically induced structural changes will heal or reduce micro-voids.
Deep cryogenic treatment promotes enhanced dislocation mobility in SLM CoCrFeNiMn.
Deep cryogenic treatment refines the microstructure and homogenizes grain size.
Microstructural refinement produced by the treatment reduces porosity and micro-cracking.
Reducing porosity, micro-cracking, and residual stress will improve the mechanical integrity of the components.
Reducing fabrication defects and residual stress will improve dimensional accuracy.
Treated components will have improved tensile strength relative to untreated SLM components.
Treated components will have improved fatigue resistance relative to untreated SLM components.
Treated components will have lower porosity and better geometric accuracy than untreated SLM components.
A gradual warm-up to room temperature prevents thermal shock after cryogenic immersion.
The efficacy of deep cryogenic treatment depends strongly on treatment duration and warming rate.
Incorrect treatment calibration may cause embrittlement or suboptimal microstructural changes.
